name: native-memory
title: Native .NET memory store replacing the pinned sqlite-memory extension

ownerGateReview.note: 15/15 approve; three notes refined scope (S2 access model + part-2 inspect, D5 default local model, D9 watcher to part 2)

in: One memory.db per install scope; all metadata (rating, access counts, provenance, workspace lifecycle, settings, sync state) as tables inside it; raccoon_meta.db deleted
Trust-first access control: memory surface read-only by default; rw/destructive access granted per project or globally via configuration
Pluggable embeddings via Microsoft.Extensions.AI IEmbeddingGenerator; memory_configure gains provider + baseUrl + model + apiKey
Default local embedding engine = small downloaded in-process model (all-MiniLM, ONNX Runtime); any OpenAI-compatible endpoint replaceable
Hybrid search = FTS5 + sqlite-vec fused with reciprocal rank fusion (k default 60, swept 10-60; weights default 1:1), ranking normalized to 0..1
Golden-retrieval harness gating the extension swap (nDCG parity delta <= 0.02, no degenerate-query regression, p95 latency)
Workspaces as first-class entities: entries.workspace_id FK + XOR CHECK, lifecycle Active/Closed in-bank, consolidate/discard in one transaction
Content identity = path-scoped SHA-256(path + value); global content dedup preserved (write-once, share via distinct path, consolidation keeps path)
Own sync: one snapshot file per install scope to S3-compatible storage (R2/S3/MinIO), VACUUM INTO + integrity check + If-Match CAS + row merge (updated_at LWW + tombstones); workspace rows never sync
MCP surface parity: 17 tools unchanged in name and parameters
out: Unified multi-source question answering (SmartRAG-style text-to-SQL across databases, OCR, transcripts) — the agent is the integrator
Semantic Kernel and Microsoft.Extensions.VectorData connectors as dependencies
sqliteai native extensions (sqlite-memory, sqlite-vector, sqlite-sync/cloudsync) and download-on-first-run provisioning
Metrics and tracing for memory operations (part 2)
Existing-bank migration (fresh start; re-hash + re-embed migration only if a deployment later needs it)
Retrieval-mode strategy bands (keyword/vector/hybrid routing — later, behind the same memory_search contract)
REST/HTTP management API, auth beyond configuration-gated access, web UI

nonFunctional: Clean layering: domain (Core) free of SQLite/HTTP dependencies; MCP layer stays thin; SQL confined to Infrastructure
High-performance logging: static partial Log with [LoggerMessage] methods
No hardcoded secrets: AIRACCOON_SYNC_* and provider keys from environment only; repo scan finds no credentials
WAL + busy_timeout on every connection; sync serialized per project (SemaphoreSlim + lockfile)
VACUUM INTO snapshot before upload; PRAGMA integrity_check before any replace; snapshot uploads never corrupt the cloud copy
Tombsone GC strictly below the minimum of both installs' last_pull watermark
TDD mandatory: behavior tests before implementation, scenario tests pinning dedup/share/consolidation semantics
TreatWarningsAsErrors; dotnet build + dotnet test green

packages: Microsoft.Extensions.AI.OpenAI 10.8.3 (endpoint override for any OpenAI-compatible provider)
HiraokaHyperTools.sqlite-vec 0.1.9 (or own provisioning of sqlite-vec v0.1.9)

targets.implementation: src/AiRaccoon.Infrastructure (SQLite schema, search, embedding, sync) + src/AiRaccoon.Core (domain)

risks: sqlite-vec is pre-v1 ('expect breaking changes') — pin version and re-run the harness on upgrade
linux-musl gap: sqlite-vec NuGet natives and ONNX Runtime musl coverage unverified — verify at build time
RRF k is corpus-scale-dependent — the harness sweeps k and weights rather than assuming 60
Engine change forces a one-time full re-embed of the bank
Delete propagation correctness is the highest-risk merge surface — dedicated tombstone tests required

deferred.fallback: Part 2, separate task; watches table added with it
Part 2; the trust-first access model ships in V1 core
